steps.body:
In C2 you split a journey into legs by hand, measured each one, and added the lengths as positive numbers. That was hard work.

Here is the machine that does it:

**Displacement = ∫ₐᵇ v dt** — where you ended up.
**Total distance = ∫ₐᵇ |v| dt** — every metre you actually covered.

The absolute value does *exactly* the leg-splitting you did by hand. It was never a different idea; it was the same idea, automated.

explanationVariants: An antiderivative of t² − 4t + 3 is t³/3 − 2t² + 3t. At 4 it is 64/3 − 32 + 12 = 4/3; at 0 it is 0. So the displacement is 4/3 ≈ 1.333.
The signed integral does not care about the backtracking — that is precisely what makes it displacement rather than distance.

widget.prompt: v(t) = t² − 4t + 3 on [0, 4]. Find the DISPLACEMENT, to three decimals.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the TOTAL DISTANCE. The displacement is the SIGNED integral, and the backward stretch cancels part of the forward: 4/3 ≈ 1.333.
Check the antiderivative at 4: 64/3 − 32 + 12 = 4/3, not 0. (It IS 0 at t = 3, which is a different time.)
That is 64/3 — you evaluated t³/3 alone and dropped the −2t² + 3t.

widget.prompt: A velocity that starts NEGATIVE and turns positive. Drag to the instant where the accumulated displacement stops falling.
widget.successFeedback: At the moment v crosses zero, the accumulation is flat — the particle has stopped reversing and is about to go forward again. Before it, the area under v was BELOW the axis and counted negative; after it, positive. That signed accounting IS displacement, and the total distance is what you get by refusing to let any of it count negative.
widget.lowFeedback: v is still negative here, so the displacement is still falling. Keep going right.
widget.highFeedback: Past the crossing — v has turned positive and the displacement is climbing again. Come back left.

cml.actionGoal: Move an upper bound and coordinate accumulated area with the integrand's current value.

predict.prompt: The velocity starts negative and later turns positive. The accumulated displacement stops falling at the instant when…

options.label: The velocity is at its most negative
The object gets back to where it started

predict.reveal: When v hits zero. Displacement falls exactly while v is negative, so the turn is where v crosses the axis — not where the object happens to return, and not where it is moving fastest backwards. That crossing is also the moment displacement and total distance stop agreeing.

explanationVariants: |v| changes formula wherever v changes SIGN. v = (t − 1)(t − 3) is zero at t = 1 and t = 3, so [0, 4] splits into three pieces.
You cannot integrate |v| in one go — you must find the sign changes first, exactly as you found the turning points by hand in C2.

widget.prompt: v(t) = (t − 1)(t − 3). To compute ∫₀⁴ |v| dt, into how many pieces must the interval be split?

commonErrors.feedback: v changes sign TWICE — at t = 1 and at t = 3 — which cuts [0, 4] into three pieces: [0,1], [1,3] and [3,4].
|v| has a different formula on each stretch where v has a different sign, and there are three such stretches.
Two sign changes make three pieces, not four.

widget.fallbackFeedback: v changes sign at t = 1 and t = 3, giving three pieces.

steps.body:
So the recipe for total distance is exactly the hand method, written down:

**Find where v = 0 and changes sign.** (the turns)
**Integrate v on each piece.**
**Add the ABSOLUTE VALUES.**

And that is why ∫|v| is not a strange new integral — it is three ordinary integrals with the minus signs stripped off.

explanationVariants: The three pieces give 4/3, −4/3 and 4/3. Taking absolute values: 4/3 + 4/3 + 4/3 = 4.
The middle leg is negative — the particle was reversing — and stripping its sign is what turns displacement into distance.

widget.prompt: The three legs of ∫v dt come out as 4/3, −4/3 and 4/3. Find the TOTAL DISTANCE travelled.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the DISPLACEMENT: 4/3 − 4/3 + 4/3 = 4/3, with the signs left in. Distance strips them: 4/3 + 4/3 + 4/3 = 4.
The legs cancel only if you keep the signs. Total distance takes the ABSOLUTE VALUE of each: 4.
That is two legs' worth. There are three, each of magnitude 4/3, so the total is 4.

hints: Average VELOCITY is displacement ÷ elapsed time. Average SPEED is total distance ÷ elapsed time.
The displacement is 4/3 and the total distance is 4, over 4 seconds.
So the two averages are (4/3)/4 and 4/4 — and they are wildly different.
explanationVariants: Average speed = 4/4 = 1, while average velocity = (4/3)/4 = 1/3. The particle covered ground three times faster than it made progress.
That gap is the whole distinction: velocity is about where you ended up; speed is about how hard you worked.

widget.prompt: Displacement 4/3, total distance 4, over 4 seconds. Find the AVERAGE SPEED.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the average VELOCITY: displacement ÷ time = (4/3)/4 = 1/3. Average SPEED uses the distance: 4/4 = 1.
That is the total distance. Divide by the elapsed time, 4 seconds.
That is the displacement itself. Average speed = distance ÷ time = 4/4 = 1.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Average speed = total distance ÷ time = 4/4 = 1. (Average velocity is only 1/3 — the particle covered ground three times faster than it made progress.)

steps.body: The absolute value does the leg-splitting.
takeaways: To compute ∫|v|, find where v changes sign, integrate on each piece, and add the MAGNITUDES.
It is not a new idea — it is the hand method from C2, written as a machine.
steps.teaser: That is what the integral is FOR. Next course: differential equations, where the rate is all you are given.

concept.body: Two questions, two integrals. **Where did it end up?** — integrate v, signs and all. **How far did it travel?** — integrate |v|, which means splitting at the sign changes and adding the magnitudes.

explanationVariants: Total distance counts every metre, forwards and backwards, so it needs ∫|v| dt.
The plain ∫v would let the backtracking cancel.

widget.prompt: Which integral gives the TOTAL DISTANCE travelled?

options.label: ∫|v| dt
options.feedback: Right — the absolute value stops the backward stretches from cancelling the forward ones.

options.label: ∫v dt
options.feedback: That is the DISPLACEMENT. Backward travel subtracts from it, which is exactly what distance must not allow.
